[[1]](#ref-1) The reclamation project, initiated by wealthy merchants and city officials from nearby Amsterdam and other towns, involved the construction of dikes and windmills to pump out water, transforming the former lake into fertile agricultural land. [[2]](#ref-2) Hydraulic engineer and millwright Jan Adriaanszoon Leeghwater (1575–1650), a native of nearby De Rijp, played a prominent advisory role in such projects across North Holland, including the Purmer, and his influence is commemorated locally.

seltz.snippet:
The Purmerkerk is a church in the Purmerpolder, in the municipality of Purmerend, in the Dutch province of Noord-Holland. It is a Dutch Reformed church. The church is in the village annex neighborhood of Purmerbuurt.

The old Purmerkerk was built in 1864/1865, taking the church in Sloten as an example. The construction cost almost 29,000 guilders. In 1959 the church burned down and poured the largest part of the church. It was decided to demolish the remaining walls and the remaining remains of the tower.

The current Purmerkerk is a church built in 1960/1961 as a replacement for the Purmer brand burned down in 1959. The architect was Berend Tobia Boeyinga. The building is built in the form of a Greek cross and has recesses in the cube shapes. The bottom of the church consists of red bricks and the top is plastered white. On the left side of the building is the Christ Monogram depicted, an X (the Greek letter Chi) and a P (the Greek letter Rho), which is also found above the pulpit. The small tower on the top of the church was fired with copper. On the inside the roof is painted blue and white. The church has an oak wood interior. In addition, a church building was built in which there is a kitchen.

Next to the church is the parsonage that survived the 1959 fire. Since 1865 there have been ministers here. First of the old (burned) Purmerkerk and later of the current Purmerkerk.

There is also a monument to the church that was founded by the church council together with the Purmerbelang organization for victims of World War II after the war. On May 4, wreaths are laid and a small service is held. Externe link 52° 29′ 47″ NB, 4° 59′ 7″ OL
